summary: On May 25, 2003, a Boeing 727-223 registered as N844AA was stolen from Quatro de Fevereiro Airport in Luanda, Angola. Mechanics Ben Charles Padilla and John Mikel Mutantu were aboard when the aircraft taxied without tower clearance, maneuvered erratically, and took off heading southwest over the Atlantic Ocean with its transponder off. Neither the aircraft nor the two men were ever seen again, sparking a worldwide intelligence hunt involving the FBI and CIA.
research_points: The history of aircraft N844AA, including its transition from American Airlines to Aerospace Sales & Leasing and its prolonged grounding in Luanda.
The background and motives of American flight engineer Ben Charles Padilla and Congolese mechanic John Mikel Mutantu.
The exact timeline of events on May 25, 2003, including air traffic control radio contact failure and erratic runway taxiing.
The post-9/11 global security response and international search efforts conducted by U.S. intelligence agencies across Africa.
Leading theories regarding the disappearance: an ocean crash, clandestine dismantling for scrap, fuel exhaustion, or use in illegal charter operations.
title: The Vanishing Airliner: How a Boeing 727 Was Stolen and Lost Forever
description: On May 25, 2003, a massive Boeing 727 lined up on a runway in Luanda, Angola, took off into the evening sky without clearance, and completely vanished from the face of the Earth. Aboard were two men who were not certified pilots. In the wake of 9/11, this baffling heist triggered a frantic global hunt by the CIA and FBI. How does a 100-ton commercial jet disappear without leaving a single trace? In this episode of Shadow Archive, we examine the timeline, the chief suspects, and the lingering theories behind history's most audacious aviation disappearance.
